findings.what: ED220-TOPLEVEL-DEFAULT-HOLLOW is still partial: the top-level default check accepts invented role IDs containing `president` or `alex-alpha` as valid President identity values.
findings.why: `deriveBinding` gates `rb.top_level_human_default` with `isPresidentIdentity`, and that helper returns true for any normalized role containing `president` or `alexalpha`. A trusted-kernel value like `fake-president-role`, `president-worker`, or `alex-alpha-bogus` therefore returns ok:true and binds that bogus top-level role instead of failing closed. The claimed fix requires a bogus top_level_human_default to BLOCK, not merely to contain a President-looking substring.

findings.what: Legacy-signature acceptance still allows verdict flips on legacy-signed records that carry a `verdict` field.
findings.why: `verifyRecord` accepts `LEGACY_SIGNED_FIELDS` unconditionally. A record signed over the legacy field set with `verdict:"fail"` still verifies after changing the verdict to `pass`, because `verdict` is ignored by that accepted legacy canonical string. This preserves backcompat, but the comment/claim that sign-the-verdict fully closes post-hoc verdict flips needs a versioned boundary or legacy acceptance limited to records with no verdict field.

parsed.summary: Round-1 bridge fail-closed behavior is materially improved: corrupt/value-failed controls, missing resolver, President aliases, and unsigned gauntlet records are refused in the checked paths. However the top-level default validation still accepts bogus President-looking role IDs, so the Round-1 ED220 top-level-default finding is not fully closed. Direct in-process tests for resolver/signing/authority scan passed; `node --test` itself is blocked in this sandbox by spawn EPERM.
